key_insight: Independent benchmarking of open-source thigh muscle MRI segmentation tools found large performance differences, with domain-specific models generally outperforming foundation and general-purpose architectures.
clinical_relevance: More accurate and usable muscle MRI segmentation can improve biomarker extraction for neuromuscular disease research, but weak performance on pathological cases could distort interpretation if deployed uncritically.
method: Compared 8 open-source segmentation tools, including 6 standalone models and 2 auxiliary label-refinement methods.
Evaluated 3D MRI volumes from three base datasets and additional derived datasets.
Assessed both quantitative accuracy metrics and qualitative usability across methods.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports substantial variation in performance across methods and datasets, with reduced accuracy on pathological cases and consistent gains for domain-specific models trained on larger datasets.
watch_item: Tools may not generalize well to underrepresented populations or disease patterns, so external validation on local data is essential before adoption.
paper_title: Benchmarking open-source automated thigh muscle MRI segmentation algorithms
